intro: Flovilla sits right against Indian Springs State Park, and that adjacency shapes its opossum calls: the park's Big Sandy Creek and McIntosh Lake habitat keeps a steady supply of Virginia opossums moving onto the surrounding rural-residential lots. Most of the trouble is at or below grade — under a porch, in a crawlspace, or inside a shed or barn. The good news for a Flovilla homeowner is that a yard opossum just passing through usually needs nothing at all; it is the one that has moved under a structure that calls for trapping and exclusion.
extendedBody:
Why Opossums Turn Up Around Flovilla Homes

The Virginia opossum is common throughout central Georgia and breeds across most of the year here, so there is no single season when it stops appearing. In a place the size of Flovilla — a small rural community of a few hundred people hard against Indian Springs State Park — the source is rarely a mystery. The park's wooded acreage along Big Sandy Creek and the 105-acre McIntosh Lake holds a continuous opossum population, and animals filter out from that habitat onto the adjacent rural-residential lots looking for the easiest food and shelter they can find.

Where They Settle In

An opossum is an opportunist, not a digger, and it takes whatever sheltered, ground-level space is already open: a crawlspace with a missing vent screen, the void under a deck or porch, or — very common on Flovilla's rural-acreage lots — a barn, shed, or equipment building. Because opossums are wanderers rather than territory-holders, the same opening tends to be reused by one animal after another until it is finally closed.

Before You Trap: Many Flovilla Opossums Are Worth Leaving

An opossum crossing the yard at night is usually doing more good than harm, and it is worth knowing why before you call for removal:

  • Its naturally low body temperature makes it a poor host for rabies — opossums are among the least likely mammals in Georgia to carry it.
  • It grooms off and eats large numbers of ticks, a genuine benefit on tick-heavy lots near the park.
  • It preys on mice, rats, insects, and carrion, helping hold down the rodents that in turn draw snakes.

A yard-only opossum with no way under a structure generally moves along within a few weeks on its own. The animal that warrants action is the one that has denned under the house, under a deck, or in an outbuilding — that is when droppings, odor, and torn insulation start, and that is the situation worth removing and sealing.

Keeping Them Out — Across Every Structure on the Lot

Because opossums use existing gaps rather than excavating, exclusion is mostly a matter of closing openings — and on a Flovilla rural property that means thinking past just the house:

  • Screen the openings — crawlspace vents, skirting gaps, and the perimeter under decks and porches — with 1/4-inch hardware cloth, buried a few inches and turned outward so a digging animal cannot follow the opossum in.
  • Close the outbuildings too. Barns, sheds, and equipment buildings are prime dens here; seal their ground-level gaps along with the house.
  • Cut the draw — latch trash lids, bring pet food in overnight, and clear fallen fruit and spilled birdseed.
  • Confirm empty first. Nothing gets sealed until the space is checked for an animal or a female carrying young, so nothing is closed in. Trapping and removal are carried out under Georgia DNR Wildlife Resources Division practice.

faqs.q: What does opossum removal cost in Flovilla, GA?
faqs.a: It depends on where the animal is and how many openings have to be closed. A single opossum trapped from under a porch is at the low end; a rural Flovilla property where the house plus a barn or shed all need sealing runs higher because the work is the exclusion, not the trapping. A quick inspection gives an accurate number.

faqs.q: Is the opossum under my Flovilla house dangerous?
faqs.a: Not very. Opossums rarely carry rabies because of their low body temperature, and they are not aggressive — the hiss and gape are a bluff. The real issues with one denned under a structure are droppings, odor, and disturbed insulation, which is why an under-structure animal should be removed and the access sealed.

faqs.q: Why do opossums keep getting under my Flovilla house?
faqs.a: Because Flovilla borders Indian Springs State Park, and the park's Big Sandy Creek and McIntosh Lake habitat keeps a steady opossum population moving onto nearby lots. They reuse any open crawlspace, under-deck void, or outbuilding gap until it is physically closed, so sealing the access is what ends the cycle.

faqs.q: Will the opossum in my yard just leave on its own?
faqs.a: If it is only passing through the yard and has no den under a structure, usually yes — within a few weeks once it works through the local food and shelter. The one to act on is the opossum living under the house, deck, or an outbuilding.

faqs.q: What time of year are opossums active around Flovilla?
faqs.a: All year. Opossums breed across most of the year in central Georgia, so they turn up in every season, with a noticeable bump in summer when that year's juveniles strike out on their own and wander into garages and sheds.
